title: Epic Veggie Dumpling Goddess Bowl
subtitle: with Edamame and Japanese Dressing
description: All hail the Goddess Bowl! Just in time for easier, peasier and lush-er summer eating, this vegetarian PLUS recipe nails the yum-factor right on the head. We’re in love with the flavour overload of this amazing dish, from the crispy dumplings, avo, Japanese dressing and coriander to our fave salad veggies.

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Check your avocado is ripe before starting this recipe (see Cooking tip). Bring a small saucepan of salted water to the boil for the edamame. Thinly slice the radish with a sharp knife or mandoline, then put in a bowl of iced water to crisp up. Halve the tomatoes. Pick the coriander leaves and finely chop the stems.

Cook edamame: Put the tomatoes, coriander stems and a pinch of sugar in a bowl, season with salt and pepper and toss to combine. Add the edamame to the pan of boiling water. Return to the boil and cook for 2 mins. Remove from the pan with a slotted spoon. Return the water to the boil.
Boil eggs: Add 2 eggs to the pan of boiling water and cook for 6 mins for soft-boiled, or 8 mins for hard-boiled. Drain, then cool in cold water. Peel and halve the eggs.

Cook dumplings: Heat 1 tbs vegetable oil in a medium frypan over medium-high heat. Cook the dumplings, without turning, for 2-3 mins until golden on one side. Carefully add 60ml (¼ cup) water and 2 tsp soy sauce (take extra care adding water to the hot pan as the oil can spit and the steam created is very hot). Cover and steam for 3 mins or until the dumplings are tender.

Serve up: Thinly slice the avocado (see Kitchen hack). Divide the dumplings, egg, edamame, radish, tomatoes and avocado among bowls. Drizzle with the Japanese dressing, scatter over the sesame seeds and coriander leaves and enjoy!

Kitchen hack: Want to curl the avocado into 'roses' like we've done in the photo? Peel the avocados, then halve and remove the stones. Put one half, cut-side down, on a board. Very thinly slice the avocado crosswise. Fan out the slices to make a straight line, then turn it into a horseshoe shape. Starting at one end, curl the slices inwards to make a spiral 'rose'. Repeat with the remaining avocado halves.
